To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SEA process should systematically include components for explicit gap handling, monitoring and adaptive governance, which is especially needed for the Arctic region.
SEA should be applied to identify and systematically handle knowledge gaps and uncertainties and to formulate and promote necessary new and modified monitoring objectives for reducing them.

SEA should be applied as a systematic framework for the identification and efficient reduction (e.g., by bridging gaps) of uncertainties in the environmental change knowledge base, and for the promotion of necessary new or modified environmental monitoring activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the application of environmental monitoring within the context of SEA, and we provide an overarching framework for SEA that explicitly addresses key knowledge and information needs, and the related monitoring, to support decision making on environmental management and governance in the rapidly changing Arctic.
the development and application of a systematic framework for SEA and monitoring in the Arctic region, with focus on bridging the gaps and uncertainties of environmental change and its impacts.

bridging key knowledge and information (i.e., monitoring) gaps in the application of SEA in the Arctic region, which is a key step towards more efficient and effective environmental management in this region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SEA and monitoring are two sides of the same coin.

strategic environmental assessment is an overarching framework that can systematically link the monitoring of environmental changes to the decision-making processes and thus contribute to the sustainable development of the Arctic region.
the Arctic region is in urgent need of improved and more integrated environmental assessment and monitoring, and that this can be achieved through the proposed SEA framework.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SEA and monitoring are complementary tools to support decision making in the context of environmental change.

SEA should systematically and explicitly consider the monitoring of environmental changes as part of the SEA process, including the identification of gaps in monitoring and the development of strategies for their bridging.
the overarching SEA framework is a key pathway for bridging the gaps between environmental change and its impacts on society and the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

SEA should systematically include and explicitly handle environmental observations and their gaps, and that the SEA process can be an important tool in identifying key gaps in environmental observations and in promoting and guiding the development of monitoring strategies to reduce these gaps.

SEA and monitoring must go hand in hand, and that SEA must be applied to identify and reduce gaps in monitoring, as well as to systematically link and integrate monitoring with other steps of the SEA.
SEA is a powerful instrument to improve monitoring and its outcomes in the Arctic and elsewhere.
